name: native-e2e-ci
body: Native e2e CI job: a GitHub Actions matrix with one GitHub-hosted native runner per supported target: darwin/arm64 on an Apple silicon runner (`macos-14`/`macos-latest`), darwin/amd64 on an Intel macOS runner (`macos-15-intel`/`macos-26-intel`), windows/amd64 on `windows-latest`, windows/arm64 on `windows-11-arm`, linux/amd64 on `ubuntu-latest`/`ubuntu-24.04`, linux/arm64 on `ubuntu-24.04-arm` — each job runs on a GitHub-hosted runner when GitHub currently offers that runner to the repo (a target whose runner is unavailable is omitted, per supported-platforms). Each job runs against its target's built `kalide-<os>-<arch>` binary (located via `KALIDE_BINARY`). Steps: in a clean temp dir, `kalide init`, then `kalide start --no-open` in the background in its own process group; parse the printed URL; poll until HTTP 200 with the seed's single `hello` slide (timeout about 30s); fetch the reveal.js runtime (embedded core) and the project theme stylesheet (from `templates/themes/default/`) and confirm both are served by the local server; enforce offline operation by blocking or disabling outbound network for the process or asserting that the process makes no outbound connections (mechanism chosen per OS); stop it with SIGTERM to the process group on macOS and Linux (Linux jobs reuse the existing Unix process-group/lsof offline and shutdown mechanism, same as macOS) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT to the process group on Windows, then assert exit code 0, port released and every child process reaped. Graceful shutdown within the timeout is required; a forced timeout kill fails the job.
